body: This should really be the top include swapped with `editor_export.h`

```suggestion
	patch_delta_zstd_level->set_tooltip_text(vformat(TTR(
```
`vformat` needs to go around `TTR`, or it won't work as it can't translate the text with replacements already done

```suggestion
			"Level 0 will cause Zstandard to use its default compression level, which is currently level %d."),
			ZSTD_CLEVEL_DEFAULT));
```
I had completely missed that it was the main header of that file. Nice catch.
clang-format did not like this arrangement, so I formatted things a bit differently.

A silly thing to push back against, and I realize single quotes is a bit of a programmer-ism to begin with, but if consistency is the goal here then it might be worth pointing out that usage of `'%s'` in the codebase outnumbers `"%s"` by quite a bit (roughly double).

Given that, do you still want me to change these?
The current push has been for double quotes and is generally used for new code, but we can leave it here
I went ahead and changed it.

body:
That's not how `bundle` works, it is supposed to have file content outside `.pack` stored by its original name, which won't work for patches (since file name is the same for both base and patch).

I guess we can make some system for this, but I would just fail if `delta_patch.bundle` is set, since there's no condition when patch pack with `bundle` can be written.

body: I went ahead and threw in an `ERR_FAIL_COND_V` for that condition.

I guess it made more sense back when I had some more stuff in the header, as I used to store checksums there as well, but it was simply to avoid having a bunch of hardcoded offsets and pointer arithmetic that can get screwed up in any number of ways (if the header changes in some way).

I guess it isn't really that bad with what little is in there now, so I've removed the struct in favor of the hardcoded offsets.
